newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo central bank takes steps to save the dinar.
newsitem.headline: Yugo central bank takes steps to save the dinar.

text.p: The Yugoslav central bank said it had taken steps to stabilise the dinar and restore financial discipline, after its board of governors met on Friday.
"The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) Board of Governors at its session discussed the financial and monetary situation in the country," it said in a statement faxed to Reuters.

"NBY took special measures to halt further increases in the money supply, prevent imbalances on the banks' giro-accounts, halt insolvent banks from further lending activity and take other measures to establish financial discipline," it said.
A source close to the central bank told Reuters this marked only the beginning of the NBY's action to save the dinar.
The source said: "NBY will look at the effects of those steps during next week, and if they are not sufficient NBY will resort to even harsher measures, including liquidation of insolvent banks."
The dinar's plunge started during the eight-day New Year and Christmas holidays, when banks and companies were closed.
Economists and financial analysts said the dinar dived to as low as 4.3 to the mark on a sudden flood of notes put in circulation during the last few days of 1996.
Some economists blamed the government of Serbia for putting pressure on the National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) to resort to the presses and print money to ensure pensions were paid.
Others said the money was needed to cover huge imbalances of the two largest commercial banks.
Analysts estimated between 500 million and one billion dinars were printed for those purposes.
Some insisted it was the debtors lobby attempting to push the dinar down and erase its liabilities.
Yugoslavia's government, in its 1997 economic policy paper, has pledged currency stability and the dinar fixed at 3.3 to the mark. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
